scenes.text: It's December 1719, and the busiest street in Paris is a narrow lane, rue Quincampoix.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: Dukes, maids and shoemakers are fighting to buy one thing: shares in your company.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: A share that cost five hundred livres two years ago now sells for ten thousand.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: People who were poor last month are now called a brand-new word: millionaire.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: You run the bank. You run the company. Soon you'll run the entire finances of France.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And you're not even French. You're a Scottish gambler who killed a man in a duel.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In one year, all of it will be worthless, and you'll flee the country.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that got you here, and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to get here, we have to go back. It's 1671, and you're born in Edinburgh, Scotland.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: Your name is John Law. Keep count of two things: the money, and the paper.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: Your father, William, is a goldsmith. In Scotland, that also makes him a banker.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: People leave gold with him for safekeeping, and he hands them a paper receipt.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

paper.text: RECEIVED: 100 POUNDS IN GOLD. W. LAW

scenes.text: Then something interesting happens. People start paying each other with the receipts.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: The gold never moves. Only the paper does. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: You're good at numbers. Very good. Especially odds.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: He even buys an estate near Edinburgh called Lauriston. You are John Law of Lauriston.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: Your father dies when you're twelve, and leaves you a decent inheritance.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: You leave school and head for London with it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: In London, you're tall, handsome, and very good at cards.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: They call you Beau Law: beau means a fashionable dandy.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: You calculate odds at the gambling tables while everyone else just hopes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: You win a lot. You also lose a lot. You lose your inheritance.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: Gambling is fine for a gentleman. Losing everything is just embarrassing.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: Then you get into a quarrel with another dandy, Edward Wilson.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: Nobody knows exactly what the fight was about. Possibly a woman.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: On April 9th, 1694, you meet in Bloomsbury Square with swords.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: One thrust. Wilson dies on the spot.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Bloomsbury Square in London at dawn, 1694: grand brick townhouses, gravel square, iron railings, morning mist

scenes.text: You're arrested for murder.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The court finds you guilty and sentences you to hang.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The King reduces it to a fine, but Wilson's family appeals.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you escape from prison and get on a boat to the Netherlands.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Some historians think the escape was quietly arranged. Either way, you're gone.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In Amsterdam, you find the most advanced bank in Europe.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: The Bank of Amsterdam keeps coins in its vault and lets merchants pay with entries in a book.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: Trade moves faster. Credit is cheap. The Dutch are rich.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: Next door, shares of the Dutch East India Company trade every single day.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: Paper shares of a company, bought and sold like bread. You watch closely.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: You start to wonder: what if the problem in poor countries is just not enough money?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: Not enough gold and silver to go around, so nobody can trade.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: But paper can be printed. Remember your father's receipts?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: This is the idea that will shape your whole life.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of the Bank of Amsterdam, 1700: tall arched windows, heavy wooden counters, ledgers and coin scales, canal houses outside

scenes.text: Meanwhile you need to eat, so you gamble across Europe for the next twenty years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: Venice. Genoa. Paris. The Hague. Turin.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: You often play as the bank: the house that takes everyone's bets.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: Because you understand the odds, the house usually wins.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: Several cities throw you out for winning too much.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: Players say you calculate the odds of a game faster than anyone at the table.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: You meet Lady Katherine Knollys, who leaves her husband for you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: You never formally marry, but you raise two children together.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: By now, you're rich again: well over a hundred thousand pounds, by some estimates.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: But you don't want to be a gambler. You want to fix a whole country's money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Venetian gambling salon (ridotto), 1710s: candlelit room, card tables with green cloth, masks on a side table, gilded mirrors

scenes.text: In 1705, you go home and pitch Scotland a bank that issues paper money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: You publish a book: Money and Trade Considered.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Money is not the value for which goods are exchanged, but the value by which they are exchanged.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Money is not the value for which goods are exchanged, but the value by which...

scenes.text: In other words: money is a tool for trading, not treasure to hoard.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Domestic trade depends on the money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Domestick trade depends on the money.

scenes.text: The Scottish Parliament says no. Then Scotland joins England in 1707, and you're still wanted for murder there.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: goldsmith's shop in Edinburgh, 1680s: dark wood counter, scales, silver cups, a strongbox, small leaded windows onto a stone street

scenes.text: So what exactly are you selling? Let's use an island with apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The island grows one hundred apples a year and has one hundred coins.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So an apple costs one coin.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If coins are scarce, people can't trade, and apples rot. That's your argument.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Add paper money, and more apples get sold, picked and planted. Trade grows.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But here's the catch. Print a thousand paper coins, and the island still grows one hundred apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Now each apple costs about ten coins. That's inflation: prices rising because money is plentiful.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Paper money helps when it matches real trade. It hurts when it outruns it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Keep this island in mind. France is about to become it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In September 1715, King Louis the Fourteenth dies after seventy-two years on the throne.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: He leaves palaces, wars, and a debt of about two billion livres.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: France can barely pay the interest. Tax collectors keep a big share of the taxes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: The new king is five years old. The real ruler is his uncle, Philippe, Duke of Orleans.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: And Philippe happens to know you from the gambling tables.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: You tell him the problem isn't the debt. It's that France has no money moving.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: Give you a bank that prints paper, and trade will boom and the debt will melt.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: He's desperate enough to say yes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: In May 1716, you open the Banque Generale, a private bank in Paris.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Its paper notes can be swapped for coins anytime you like.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: And the government accepts them for taxes. So people trust them.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: It works. Trade picks up. Interest rates fall.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: In 1718, the King takes the bank over and renames it the Banque Royale.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Now it's the government's bank. And it can print notes without enough coins behind them.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Remember the island? You're about to print a lot of paper apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: In 1717, you take over a trading company with a monopoly on French Louisiana.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: You call it the Company of the West. Everyone else calls it the Mississippi Company.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: Louisiana is a huge territory around the Mississippi River.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early French settlement on the Mississippi River, 1719: muddy riverbank, a few wooden huts, swamp cypress trees with moss, a small sailing ship

scenes.text: In 1718, your company founds a small town on the river. It calls it New Orleans.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early French settlement on the Mississippi River, 1719: muddy riverbank, a few wooden huts, swamp cypress trees with moss, a small sailing ship

scenes.text: It's mostly swamp, forest and a few hundred settlers.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early French settlement on the Mississippi River, 1719: muddy riverbank, a few wooden huts, swamp cypress trees with moss, a small sailing ship

scenes.text: Your advertisements say it's full of gold, silver and gentle native allies.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early French settlement on the Mississippi River, 1719: muddy riverbank, a few wooden huts, swamp cypress trees with moss, a small sailing ship

scenes.text: There are no mountains of gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early French settlement on the Mississippi River, 1719: muddy riverbank, a few wooden huts, swamp cypress trees with moss, a small sailing ship

scenes.text: To get settlers, prisoners and orphans are shipped there, sometimes by force.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Many of them die of disease within months.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Back in Paris, your company keeps swallowing others.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: Tobacco. The East India trade. The China trade. The mint. Tax collection.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: Then you offer to take over the entire national debt.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: People can swap their government bonds for company shares. And they can buy shares with your bank's paper.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: The bank prints notes. The notes buy shares. The shares push the price up.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Which makes people want more shares. Which makes the bank print more notes.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Shares go from five hundred livres to ten thousand in about six months.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: New shares can be bought with a small down payment, and the rest paid later.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: So people buy far more shares than they can actually afford.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: Rue Quincampoix becomes an open-air stock market, packed day and night.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: Foreigners pour into Paris to speculate. Rooms in the city run out.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Soldiers block the street at night so people go home.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A servant reportedly makes enough to buy his master's carriage.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Regent's mother writes letters home describing the madness.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Everybody speaks in millions. I don't understand it at all.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Everybody speaks in millions. I don't understand it at all.

scenes.text: You're the most famous man in Europe. Princes wait in your hallway.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You buy grand houses, estates, and much of a whole neighborhood in Paris.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: On paper, you might be the richest private person in the world.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to run France's finances, you'd need to be Catholic.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So in December 1719, you convert. Problem solved.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In January 1720, you become Controller General of Finances. You're in charge of France's money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: The man who once escaped the gallows in London now runs the treasury of France.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: The crash that ruins you is less than a year away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: By early 1720, there's far more paper than anything it can buy.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Prices in Paris shoot up. Bread, rent, candles, everything.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In February 1720, you merge the bank and the company. If one falls, both fall.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Smart investors quietly sell shares and swap the notes for gold coins.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: One prince reportedly takes his notes to the bank and leaves with wagons of gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you make it illegal to own more than five hundred livres in gold or silver.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Police search houses. Neighbors report each other.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You've banned the thing your father's receipts were promising: real metal.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In May 1720, you announce that notes and shares will be cut to half their value.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Paris explodes. The decree is withdrawn within a week. The trust never comes back.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

scenes.text: In July, crowds crush each other trying to change notes at the bank. People die in the crush.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Royal Bank of France office in Paris, 1720: long wooden counter with iron grilles, piles of paper banknotes, clerks' desks, stone arches

scenes.text: Mobs attack your carriage. You need guards to cross the street.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your coachman is dragged from the carriage and beaten. You stay hidden in the Palais-Royal.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the end of 1720, shares are worth a small fraction of their peak.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Regent fires you in December. You leave France with almost nothing.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: Your houses, your estates and your shares all stay behind.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Regent's private study in the Palais-Royal, Paris, 1716: gilded wood panels, writing desk with quills and papers, tall windows, globe

scenes.text: A song goes around Paris about a man who buys shares on Monday and ends up in the poorhouse by Saturday.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: rue Quincampoix in Paris, 1719: narrow street of tall stone houses with wooden shutters, wooden stalls and benches, papers on the cobbles, hanging shop signs (blank)

paper.text: MONDAY: SHARES. TUESDAY: MILLIONS. SATURDAY: POORHOUSE.

scenes.text: You leave Paris in a borrowed carriage, with very little money and one family jewel.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You wander Europe again. Brussels, Venice, back to London.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: England pardons you for the duel. Twenty-five years too late to matter much.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your son, John, travels with you. Katherine and your daughter cannot leave France.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Katherine is stuck in France, and your property there has been seized.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you do the one thing you know will pay. You gamble.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: You play the same games you played at twenty-five, in the same city where you once ran the bank.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: You still win. Just never enough to get it all back.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: The internet says you died penniless and forgotten. You weren't forgotten.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: Visitors come to see the man who printed France, and you still argue that the idea was right.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: On March 21st, 1729, you die of pneumonia in Venice, aged fifty-seven.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: Your estate is mostly a collection of paintings, and a lot of debts.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: Years later, the philosopher Montesquieu writes about you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: Mr. Law was one of the greatest promoters of despotism ever known in Europe.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

quote.text: Mr. Law... one of the greatest promoters of despotism... ever known in Europe.

scenes.text: Despotism: unlimited power in one man's hands. Which, for one year, was you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented room in Venice, 1729: peeling plaster, a narrow bed, a card table, a window over a canal, winter light

scenes.text: France stays suspicious of banks and paper money for generations.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It doesn't get a real central bank again until 1800, under Napoleon.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So how did a Scottish fugitive end up running France?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: He had a real idea, a desperate government, and no one to tell him to stop printing.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: Your system lasted about four years. The idea behind it lasted three centuries.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, 1715: gilded arches, crystal chandeliers, polished parquet floor

scenes.text: Today, most countries use paper money with no gold behind it. Your idea won.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But central banks are built to say no to the government. You never were.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That brings us to today's money rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MONEY RULE: PRINTED MONEY ISN'T NEW WEALTH

scenes.text: More money only makes people richer if there's more stuff to buy with it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Paper can move goods faster. It can't grow apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here's what that looks like now. Say your pay rises three percent this year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If prices rise seven percent, you didn't get a raise. You got about four percent poorer.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 2008, prices in Zimbabwe were doubling roughly every day, after years of printing money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Most central banks today aim for about two percent inflation a year, not zero, and not twenty.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So watch the real number: what your money buys, not how much of it you have.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the rule isn't perfect. You were right that a little paper money can wake up a sleepy economy.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your first bank actually worked. It was the second part that went wrong.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The printing press is a tool. You just couldn't stop pressing it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

meta.thumbnail: A crowded 1719 Paris street with people waving paper shares, a mountain of banknotes; text: 'PRINTED FRANCE'
meta.description:
It's 1719. Paris is crowded with new millionaires, and every one of them is holding shares in your company.
In one year, it will all be worthless. This is the life of John Law.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.
General education only, not financial advice.

Sources:
- John Law (economist), Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Law_(economist)
- Mississippi Company, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_Company
- John Law, Money and Trade Considered (1705)
- Montesquieu, The Spirit of the Laws (1748), Book II, chapter 4
- Antoin E. Murphy, John Law: Economic Theorist and Policy-Maker (1997)
- James Buchan, John Law: A Scottish Adventurer of the Eighteenth Century (2018)
factCheck: Born April 21, 1671, Edinburgh; father William Law a goldsmith-banker, died 1683 (Wikipedia). Goldsmith receipts circulating as money is the standard history of goldsmith banking (general, not specific to William Law).

London 1690s, nickname 'Beau Law', gambled and lost his inheritance; killed Edward 'Beau' Wilson in a duel in Bloomsbury Square, April 9, 1694; convicted of murder and sentenced to death, sentence commuted to a fine, Wilson's brother appealed, Law escaped to Amsterdam (Wikipedia). Cause of the duel unclear (possibly Elizabeth Villiers): DISPUTED.

Studied the Bank of Amsterdam; gambled professionally across Europe for about twenty years; companion Lady Katherine Knollys (Seignieur), two children (Wikipedia). 'Over £100,000' wealth by 1710s is an estimate in secondary sources: DISPUTED.
1705 'Money and Trade Considered' proposed a land-backed paper money bank to the Scottish Parliament, rejected; Act of Union 1707 made him liable to arrest in England's jurisdiction (Wikipedia).
Louis XIV died September 1, 1715 after a 72-year reign; debt roughly 2-3 billion livres (sources vary; 2 billion used); Louis XV aged five; Regent Philippe II, Duke of Orleans (Wikipedia).
Banque Generale founded May 1716; notes convertible to coin and accepted for taxes; nationalized as Banque Royale December 1718 (Wikipedia).

1717 Compagnie d'Occident with Louisiana monopoly; merged into Compagnie des Indes 1719, absorbing tobacco, East India and China companies, the mint and tax farms; took over the national debt (Wikipedia, Mississippi Company).
Forced migration of prisoners and vagrants to Louisiana; high mortality (Wikipedia, Mississippi Company).

Shares rose from 500 livres to about 10,000 livres between mid- and late 1719 (Wikipedia). Rue Quincampoix trading; servant-turned-rich anecdotes are contemporary reports, details DISPUTED. Word 'millionaire' popularized in this period (commonly cited, DISPUTED as first use).
Converted to Catholicism late 1719; Controller General of Finances January 5, 1720 (Wikipedia).

1720: limits on holding gold and silver (about 500 livres), house searches; May 21, 1720 decree halving notes and shares, withdrawn days later; July 1720 crushes at the bank killed several people; dismissed and left France December 1720 (Wikipedia). Prince de Conti withdrew gold in carts (Wikipedia).

Mobs attacked Law's carriage in July 1720 and his coachman was injured; Law sheltered in the Palais-Royal (Wikipedia; details DISPUTED). Left France December 1720 with little money. Son John went with him; Katherine and daughter stayed in France.
Pardoned in England 1721; died in Venice March 21, 1729 of pneumonia, aged 57; estate mostly paintings (Wikipedia).

Montesquieu, Spirit of the Laws (1748), Book II ch. 4: 'Mr. Law, through ignorance both of a republican and monarchical constitution, was one of the greatest promoters of despotism that had ever been known in Europe.'
Elisabeth Charlotte, Duchess of Orleans, letter 1719 (as quoted in Buchan 2018 and others): 'Everybody speaks in millions... I don't understand it at all.' Wording varies by translation: DISPUTED.
Paris satirical rhyme 1720 (Monday shares, Tuesday millions, Saturday hospital/poorhouse): widely quoted.
Zimbabwe 2008: peak monthly inflation ~79.6 billion percent in November 2008, prices doubling about every 24.7 hours (Hanke & Kwok, Cato Journal 2009).
